todos.rules:
## Rules

1. A piece talks to other pieces only through contracts on the bus; never import another piece folder; other pieces' code is off limits, even for idioms: read context.md files and contracts only.
2. `piece.ts` exports one class, `export class X extends Piece({ needs: { db: sqlite }, config, emits: [SomeEvent] })` (`Piece()` when it has none); logic goes to private files in the folder.
3. `@Handle(C) async m(input: C): Promise<Out>`: the parameter is the contract instance, the return is the output; add `delivery: Delivery` only when you need the envelope id, attempt or signal.
4. `this.emit(E, payload)` only for events in `emits`; `this.request(C, input)` for any query or command (the call site is the declaration). On the memory transport events stay in one process; cross-process durable work is `this.jobs.enqueue(Command, input)` inside the transaction.
5. A business refusal is a returned `reject(status, message, { code, details })`: in a guard, or in any handler whose contract output is `rejectable(...)`. The edge renders it unchanged. `null` is not found. Throw only when the operation did not happen: it is retried, then dead-lettered; `NonRetryableError` when a retry cannot help.
6. Client retries: `idempotent: { scope }` on the route. Bus redelivery: key every effect on `delivery.envelope.id` (`this.kv.once(delivery.envelope.id, effect)` or a claim-first `INSERT OR IGNORE` side table); emits stay at-least-once. Durable or delayed work: `this.jobs.enqueue(C, input, { runAt, dedupeKey, groupKey })`, never a timer; periodic work: `@Handle(C, { every: '1m' })`.
7. Edges read with `const { params, query, headers, body } = await req.read({...})`, call one contract, and answer with `req.reply(outcome, { status, headers, etag })` or return the outcome. Admission is the route's guards and `meta`; never request a guard from a serve method. Domain pieces know no transport.
8. Config from `this.config`, I/O through the `needs` handles (`this.db`, …), `this.log`, `this.clock`, `this.ids`; never `process.env`. Transactions: `await this.db.transaction(async (tx) => …)`; a nested call joins. Field initialisers may use `this.db` / `this.config` / `this.log` (`readonly #repo = new Repo(this.db);`); `new X()` of the piece outside the runtime throws, tests use `testPiece`.
9. Return plain objects that satisfy the model type, never `new Model(…)`; no `typeof` types in piece code, name the class.
10. Style: every `if`/`for`/`while` body in braces; every statement ends with `;`; a blank line around blocks, after a run of two or more consts and before `return` unless it is the only statement; a single one-line `const` (even `const x = await …;`) stays attached to the block that reads it (no blank line between `const row = await …;` and `if (row === undefined) {`); a multi-line `await` statement is its own paragraph, one-line awaits group without blank lines; exported functions and class methods declare their return type; no `any`, no `!`; no statement ternaries, no `cond && call()`, no nested ternaries; no comments in bodies (knowledge goes to `context.md`).
11. One concept, one owner of its storage; ctx tiers large 25k / warn 40k / fail 80k tokens, ~1,500 lines, ~20 handlers; heuristics in `../../../../../docs/piece-authoring.md`:
    1. describable in one sentence without "and"
    2. one writer of each table; readers declare the table in context.md
    3. things that change together live together
    4. handlers sharing no state or helpers are a split smell
    5. start coarse, split on pain, never speculatively
12. Shared pure code lives in `lib/` and is imported as `#lib/x`; a capability is I/O or state, never a helper bag.

todos.capabilities:
## Capabilities

### db (sqlite)

# sqlite

The sqlite handle: one node:sqlite connection per process behind an async mutex. The piece names the field
(`needs: { db: sqlite }` → `this.db`); the examples below call it `db`. Safe when several processes share one
file: a file database runs in WAL mode (`synchronous=NORMAL`), every transaction starts with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and
a write that finds the file locked by another process waits up to `busyTimeoutMs` instead of failing with
`database is locked` (the wait blocks this process).

- `await db.row(Todo, 'SELECT id, title, done FROM todos WHERE id = ?', id)` → `{ id: 't1', title: 'buy milk', done: true }`
  (`null` when no row); `await db.rows(Todo, sql, ...params)` → `Todo[]`. Decoded by the Model's field types:
  INTEGER 0/1 → a `z.boolean()` field, JSON TEXT → a `z.array/z.object/z.record` field, every other column as is,
  extra columns dropped. Column names equal field names: alias in SQL (`created_at AS createdAt`); a missing column
  throws naming it. No column selection, query building or relations: computed fields stay your code.
- `get/all` return plain rows keyed by column name. SQLite has no boolean type (store `0`/`1`, JSON with
  `JSON.stringify`): `await db.get(sql, id)` → `{ id: 't1', title: 'buy milk', done: 1 }` (`undefined` when no row).
- `run` → `{ changes: 1, lastInsertRowid: 1 }`; params are positional `?` values (string, number, bigint, null, Uint8Array).
- `await db.insert('todos', { id: 't1', title: 'buy milk', done: 0 })` → `'t1'`: keys are column names; it returns
  the primary key you gave, else `lastInsertRowid` as a number.
- `run/get/all/rows/row/exec/insert` are async; each waits for any open transaction of another delivery.
- `const id = await db.transaction(async (tx) => { …; return id; })`: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, commit when the callback
  returns (its value is the result), rollback when it throws. Run statements on `tx`; `this.db.*` and `kv.once` of
  the same delivery, or awaited inside the callback, join it, and a nested `transaction(fn)` joins the outer one
  (one commit, no savepoint: the outer rollback undoes the inner writes, and a nested call that throws does not roll
  back on its own; let the error reach the outer callback). Work started elsewhere (another delivery, a timer firing
  after `onStart` returned) waits until the transaction ends.
- One DDL source: `migrations` defaults to `pieces/**/schema.sql` then `migrations/*.sql`, each file applied once in
  path order and recorded by relative path in `murmur_migrations`. Boot and `pnpm exec murmur migrate` run the same
  list under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so processes booting together apply each file once. `murmur_*` tables belong to the
  framework.
- Config: `path` (default `:memory:`; a bare path, `sqlite:./app.db` or `file:///srv/app.db`, relative to the app
  root, not the cwd), `busyTimeoutMs` (default 5000), `migrations` (globs, files or a directory of *.sql; replaces
  the default list).

```ts
import type { Sqlite } from '@murmur/node/capabilities';

export interface Sqlite {
  run(sql: string, ...params: unknown[]): Promise<SqliteRunResult>;
  get<T = Record<string, unknown>>(sql: string, ...params: unknown[]): Promise<T | undefined>;
  all<T = Record<string, unknown>>(sql: string, ...params: unknown[]): Promise<T[]>;
  rows<M extends ModelClass>(model: M, sql: string, ...params: unknown[]): Promise<InstanceType<M>[]>;
  row<M extends ModelClass>(model: M, sql: string, ...params: unknown[]): Promise<InstanceType<M> | null>;
  exec(sql: string): Promise<void>;
  insert(table: string, row: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): Promise<number | string>;
  transaction<T>(work: (tx: Sqlite) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}
```

### defaults: log, clock, ids

- `this.log.debug|info|warn|error(message, data?)`, `this.log.child(fields)`: structured, trace-tagged.
- `this.clock.now()` → `Temporal.Instant` (`toString()` is the ISO form to store, `epochMilliseconds` the number); `zonedNow(tz?)`; `sleep(ms, signal?)`.
- All framework time is this clock: kv windows and `ttlMs`, envelope `ts`, deadlines.
- `await this.clock.freeze(instant)`, `advance(ms)`, `clear()` move it only under `capabilities.clock.overridable: true` (murmur.yaml, test environments; a warning in prod): the instant lives in `murmur_clock`, every process on the file sees it, read once per delivery. Otherwise they throw.
- `this.ids.uuid()`; `this.ids.short()` → 8 chars [a-z0-9].
- Always on the piece, never declared in `needs`.
- Pure helpers from `@murmur/node/lib`: `cursor.encode(binding, position)` / `cursor.decode(binding, raw, Position)` (`Position` a zod schema of the position) for lists that take `...Paging({ max })` and answer `Page(Model)` (a tampered, foreign or wrongly shaped cursor decodes to a 400 `invalid_cursor` Rejection to return; the keyset `WHERE` is yours), `bearer`, `canonicalJson`, `sha256`.

### tests: testPiece, createTestApp

- `await using t = await testPiece(P)` fakes every need left out of `needs`: sqlite → `fakeSqlite({ schema: 'app' })` (the app's migrations; `needs: { db: await fakeSqlite({ schema: 'own' }) }` for this folder's `schema.sql` only), jobs → rows on that faked sqlite (a rolled-back transaction keeps none; `t.enqueued(C)` → `[{ input, options }]`, `await t.runJobs()` runs the due ones through this piece), kv, fetch (pass `fakeFetch(handler)`). `t.needs.<field>` is the handle; `await t.reset()` forgets emits, requests, log and jobs; `t.log`, `t.ids`, `t.clock` (frozen at `now`; `freeze/advance/clear` also move `fakeKv` windows).
- `t.fetch(request, { auth })` skips the route's guards. Admission (guards, `meta`, 401/429, idempotency) is tested on `await using app = await createTestApp()`: every piece over HTTP on a temp migrated database, `app.fetch('/path', init)`, `app.db`, `await app.reset()` (app tables, jobs, idempotency and kv rows, clock override), `await app.clock.freeze(instant)`, `await app.jobs.drain()`.

api/rest.serves:
## Serves

### Admission (web)

Guards run in this order, one at a time, before the body is read; the first `reject(…)` answers and the rest do not run:

1. `Authenticate` → `Principal` { userId, roles }
2. `RateLimit` → `Quota` { remaining } · optional: Authenticate · meta: cost = 1

- a route fills the guards' meta keys: `web.patch('/x/:id', { meta: { … } })`; a key no kept guard reads fails the boot (`guard-meta-unknown`); a guard runs after every guard in its `after` (`guard-order`).
- responseHeaders(auth): not set · log(auth): set (one `access { method, path, status, ms, traceId }` line per request).

| key | guards | auth | via |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET /todos | Authenticate, RateLimit | `Principal & Quota` | → todos.ListTodos |
| POST /todos/:id/complete | Authenticate, RateLimit | `Principal & Quota` | → todos.CompleteTodo |
| DELETE /todos/:id | Authenticate, RateLimit | `Principal & Quota` | → todos.RemoveTodo (204) |
| GET /stats | RateLimit (skip: [Authenticate]) | `Quota` | → stats.GetStats |
| POST /todos | Authenticate, RateLimit (meta: { cost: 2 }) | `Principal & Quota` | method create |
| GET /todos/:id | Authenticate, RateLimit | `Principal & Quota` | method show |

- forms: a `→ C` row is a shorthand above the class, `@Serve(web.get('/todos'), C)`: it reads params < query < JSON body into `C`'s input, requests `C` and answers its output like a returned outcome; a `method m` row decorates the method, `@Serve(web.post('/todos')) async m(req: WebRequest): Promise<HttpResult>`. Options are the binding's second argument: `web.delete('/todos/:id', { status: 204 })` (no body), `web.get('/x', { skip: [Guard] })` drops a default guard, `{ guards: [Guard] }` adds one, `web.post('/x', { idempotent: { scope: ['auth.userId', 'ip'] } })` makes client retries that send an `Idempotency-Key` header replay instead of running twice.
- match: a static segment beats `:param`, `:param` beats `/*rest`, segment by segment from the left, then the longer path wins (`/todos/search` before `/todos/:id`); a path served only for other methods answers 405, no path 404.
- read with `const { params, query, headers, body } = await req.read({ params?, query?, headers?, body? })`, each a zod object or shape: parts in that order, the first failing one answers; params/query strings are retried JSON-decoded (`'3'` → 3); the query is strict (unknown or repeated single keys fail, `z.array()` takes repeats); header keys are lower-case, a missing optional header is `null`, and `headers: { 'if-match': IfMatch }` (`IfMatch` from `murmur`) reads a strong ETag to its inner value or `null`; the body needs a JSON content type (else `mediaType`), empty is `{}`.
- answer with `return req.reply(outcome, { status, headers, etag })` or return the outcome; `etag: (body) => body.version` sends a strong ETag and a matching `If-None-Match` on GET answers 304.
- returning: an output (JSON, `status` or the route's), a `Rejection` (rendered unchanged through the envelope, its headers too), a `Response`, `undefined` (204) or `null` (404 `not_found`). Refuse in the edge with `return reject(403, message)`.

### web defaults

- `req: WebRequest` is `HttpRequest<Principal & Quota>`; a route that skips or adds guards spells its auth with class names.
- `req.headers` is a `Headers` (names case-insensitive); `req.peer` is the socket's remote address; `req.ip` is the first `X-Forwarded-For` entry when `capabilities.web.trustProxy: true` is set in murmur.yaml (or `MURMUR__CAP_WEB__TRUST_PROXY=true`), else `req.peer`.
- errors: PayloadTooLargeError → 413 `payload_too_large`, NoRouteError → 501 `not_implemented`, RequestTimeoutError → 504 `timeout`, HandlerTimeoutError → 504 `timeout`, RemoteError → 502 `upstream_failed`, anything else → 500 `internal`; the body is `{ error: { code, message, issues? }, traceId }`.

Input failures (`errors.input` of web): the first failing part of `req.read` answers.

| part | status | code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| params | 404 | `not_found` |
| query | 400 | `invalid_input` |
| headers | 400 | `invalid_input` |
| json | 400 | `invalid_input` |
| mediaType | 415 | `unsupported_media_type` |
| body | 422 | `validation_failed` |

- issues keep zod's `code` and params: `{ path, code, message, minimum?, maximum?, keys?, format? }`; a refinement's `params` are spread into its issue, the escape for codes zod cannot tell apart.
- issueCodes: `too_small` → `too_short`
- e.g. `req.read({ body: { title: z.string().min(1) } })` with `{"title":""}` answers 422: `{"error":{"code":"validation_failed","message":"title: Too small: expected string to have >=1 characters","issues":[{"path":["title"],"code":"too_short","message":"Too small: expected string to have >=1 characters","origin":"string","minimum":1,"inclusive":true}]},"traceId":"…"}`
